Muntzer asserted, That all of his Opinion, were Gods Elect: and that all the Children of their Religion were to be called the Children of God; and that all others were ungodly, and designed to Damnation. H. Nicholas affirms, That there was no knowledg of Christ nor Scripture, but in his Family. To this purpose most of them speak, that forsake the wayes of Truth; and though these swellings are but wind and vapour, yet those heights are very serviceable to the Devils purposes: who by this means confirms those whom he hath already Conquered, and then fits them out with the greater confidence to allure others; and Men are apt enough to be drawn by fair shews, and confident boastings. But I proceed.
units.tr: Here I might set Error before you in its rant and give you a taste of its high-flown strains. Montanus (vile as he was) had the confidence to call himself "the Comforter." Novatus and his brother would be no less than Moses and Aaron. The Gnostics called themselves the Illuminati. The Swinkfieldians assumed the title of the Confessors of the Glory of Christ. The Family of Love had their Gospel of the Kingdom. The Fratricelli distinguished themselves from others by the term Spiritual. Muntzer asserted that all of his opinion were God's elect, that all the children of their religion were to be called the children of God, and that all others were ungodly and destined to damnation. H. Nicholas affirms that there was no knowledge of Christ nor of Scripture except in his Family. Most of those who forsake the ways of truth speak to this purpose; and though these swellings are but wind and vapour, yet those heights are very serviceable to the Devil's purposes. By this means he confirms those whom he has already conquered, and then fits them out with greater confidence to allure others; and men are apt enough to be drawn by fair shows and confident boastings. But I proceed.

units.la: Fourthly, In stead of Argument to confirm an Errour, sometimes we have only bold Assertions, that it is Truth, and a confident condemning the contrary as an Errour; urging the danger of Mens rejecting it, backed with threatning of Hell and Damnation: and all this in the words of Scripture. To be sure they are right, and all other Men are wrong. This kind of confidence and fiercenesse hath been still the complexion of any remarkable way of Delusion; for that commonly confines their Charity to their own Party, (which is a great token of an Errour) not only may you observe in such extraordinary Proclamations of Wrath against those that will not believe them: (a practice used by the Mad Fanaticks of Munster; who, (as our Quakers were wont to do) go up and down the streets, crying, Wo, wo; Repent, repent; come out of Babylon; the heavy Wrath of God; the Axe is laid to the root of the Tree.) But in their more setled Teaching, they pronounce all to be Antichrist, and of the carnal Church, that do oppose them. Take for this H. Nicholas his words, all Knowledg (besides his) is but witchery and blindnesse, and all other Teachers, and Learners, are a false Christianity, and the Devils Synagogue; a nest of Devils, and wicked Spirits; a false Being, the Antichrist, the Kingdom of Hell, the Majesty of the Devil, &c. This piece of Art, not only our Quakers, (to whom nothing is more familiar, than to say to any opposer, Thou art Damn'd, thou art in the Gall of bitterness, the Lake of fire and brimstone is prepared for thee, &c.) but also the Papists commonly practise, who shut all out of Heaven that are not of their Church; and when they would affright any from Protestanism, they make not nice to tell him, That there is no possibility of Salvation, but in their way.
units.tr: Fourthly, instead of argument to confirm an error, sometimes we have only bold assertions that it is truth, and a confident condemning of the contrary as an error, urging the danger of men's rejecting it, backed with threatening of Hell and damnation, and all this in the words of Scripture. To be sure, they are right and all other men are wrong. This kind of confidence and fierceness has always been the complexion of any remarkable way of delusion, for it commonly confines their charity to their own party (which is a great token of an error). You may observe this not only in such extraordinary proclamations of wrath against those who will not believe them (a practice used by the mad fanatics of Munster, who, as our Quakers were wont to do, went up and down the streets crying, Woe, woe; repent, repent; come out of Babylon; the heavy wrath of God; the axe is laid to the root of the tree), but also in their more settled teaching, where they pronounce everyone who opposes them to be Antichrist and of the carnal Church. Take for this H. Nicholas his words: all knowledge (besides his) is but witchery and blindness, and all other teachers and learners are a false Christianity and the Devil's synagogue; a nest of devils and wicked spirits; a false being, the Antichrist, the kingdom of Hell, the majesty of the Devil, &c. This piece of art is commonly practised not only by our Quakers, to whom nothing is more familiar than to say to any opposer, Thou art damned, thou art in the gall of bitterness, the lake of fire and brimstone is prepared for thee, &c., but also by the Papists, who shut out of Heaven all who are not of their Church; and when they would frighten anyone from Protestantism, they do not scruple to tell him that there is no possibility of salvation but in their way.

units.la: Fifthly, 'Tis an usual trick of Satan to derive a credit and honour to Errour, from the excellencies (suppposed, or real) of the Persons that more eminently appear for it. So that it fetcheth no small strength from the qualities of those that propagate it. The Vulgar (that do not usually dive deep into the Natures of Things) content themselves with the most Superficial Arguments, and are sooner won to a good conceit of any Opinion, by the respects they carry to the Author, than by the strongest Demonstration.
units.tr: Fifthly, it is a usual trick of Satan to derive credit and honour to error from the excellencies (supposed or real) of the persons who more eminently appear for it. So it draws no small strength from the qualities of those who propagate it. The vulgar, who do not usually dive deep into the natures of things, content themselves with the most superficial arguments, and are sooner won to a good opinion of any doctrine by the regard they carry to its author than by the strongest demonstration.

units.la: But the other excellency of Holinefs in the Teachers of Errour, is more generally and more advantagioufly improved by Satan, to perswade Men, that all is true Doctrine which such Men professe. Of this Delusion Christ forewarned us, They shall come in Sheeps cloathing; that is, under the mask of seeming holinefs;* (at least at first;) notwithstanding, beware of them, Math. 7. 15. Those complained of by Paul, 2 Cor. 11.15. though they were Satans Ministers, yet that they and their Doctrine might be more plausibly entertained, they were transformed as the Ministers of Righteousnefs: this cunning we may espie in Hereticks of all ages. The Scribes and Pharisees used a pretence of Sanctity as a main piece of Art, to draw others to their way; their Alms, Fastings, long Prayers, strict Observations, &c. were all designed as a Net to catch the Multitude withal. The lying Doctrines of Antichrist were foretold by Paul, to have their succefs from this stratagem; all that Idolatry and Heathenifm which he is to introduce, must be, (and hath been) through the hypocrifie of a painted holinefs; and where he intends most to play the Dragon, he there most artificially counterfeits the innocency and simplicity of the Lamb. Arch-hereticks have been Arch-pretenders to Sanctity. And such pretences have great influence upon Men: for Holiness and Truth are so near of kin, that they will not readily believe that it can be a false Doctrine which an holy Man Teacheth; they think that God that hath given a Teacher Holiness, will not deny him Truth: Nay, this is an easie and plausible measure, which they have for Truth and Errour. To enquire into the intricacies and depths of a Disputation, is too burdensome and difficult for ordinary Men, and therefore they satisfie themselves with this consideration, (which hath little toyl in it, and as little certainty) That surely God will not leave holy Men to a delusion. It would be endless to give all the instances that are at hand in this Matter; I shall only add a few things of Satans method in managing this Argument, as
units.tr: But the other excellency, that of holiness in the teachers of error, is more generally and more advantageously exploited by Satan to persuade men that all is true doctrine which such men profess. Christ forewarned us of this delusion: "They shall come in sheep's clothing," that is, under the mask of seeming holiness (at least at first); notwithstanding, "beware of them," Matt. 7:15. Those whom Paul complains of, 2 Cor. 11:15, though they were Satan's ministers, yet, that they and their doctrine might be more plausibly received, were "transformed as the ministers of righteousness." We may observe this cunning in heretics of all ages. The scribes and Pharisees used a pretence of sanctity as a main piece of their art, to draw others to their way: their alms, fastings, long prayers, strict observances, and so on, were all designed as a net to catch the multitude. The lying doctrines of Antichrist were foretold by Paul to succeed by this stratagem: all that idolatry and heathenism which he is to introduce must be (and has been) through the hypocrisy of a painted holiness; and where he most intends to play the dragon, there he most artfully counterfeits the innocence and simplicity of the lamb. Arch-heretics have been arch-pretenders to sanctity. And such pretences have great influence upon men, for holiness and truth are so closely akin that they will not readily believe that a doctrine taught by a holy man can be false; they think that God, who has given a teacher holiness, will not deny him truth. Nay, this is an easy and plausible measure which they have for truth and error. To enquire into the intricacies and depths of a dispute is too burdensome and difficult for ordinary men, and therefore they satisfy themselves with this consideration, which has little toil in it and as little certainty: "That surely God will not leave holy men to a delusion." It would be endless to give all the instances at hand in this matter; I shall only add a few things about Satan's method in managing this argument, as follows.

units.la: Thirdly, When once Men are set in the way of exercising severities, Satan endeavours (by working upon their fancies) to press them on further to a delight and satisfaction in these {*}wayes of strictness, so that the practisers themselves are not only confirmed in these usages, and the opinions that are concomitant with them; but others are the more easily drawn to like and profess the same things. Any serious temper under any Profession of Religion, easily comes to be devout, and readily complies with opportunities of evincing its Devotion by strictness. And therefore we shall find among Heathens, a great devotional severity, and such as far exceeds all of that kind, which the Papists do usually brag of; the Magi abstained from Wine, eat not the flesh of living Creatures, and professed Virginity. The Indian Brachmans did the like, and besides used themselves to incredible hardship; they laid upon skins, sustained the violence of the Sun, and Storms, and exercised themselves therewith; some spending Thirty seven years in this course, others more. We read strange things of this nature concerning the Ægyptian Priests, and others. The Mahumetans are not without their Religious Orders, which pretend a more holy and austere Life than others; and though of some (as of the Torlachs and Dervizes) several private Villanies are reported, yet of others, (as of the Order of Calender) we are assured from History, That they profess Virginity, and expose themselves to Hardship, and a stricter Devotion in their way; and generally 'tis said, of all of them, That they go meanly clad, or half naked; some abstinent in Eating, and Drinking, professing Poverty, renouncing the World: some can endure cutting and slashing, as if they were insensible; some profess perpetual Silence, though urged with Injuries, and Tortures; others have Chains about their Necks and Arms, to shew, that they are bound up from the World, &c. If such things may be found among Heathens, no wonder that Errour boasts of them, for in both there is the same reason of Mens pleasing themselves in such hardships (which is from a Natural Devotion, assisted by Satans cunning,) and the same Design driven on by it; for the Devil doth confirm Heathens and Mahumetans in their false Worship, by the reverence and respect they carry to such practi-ces.
units.tr: Thirdly, once people are set on the path of practising severities, Satan endeavours, by working on their imaginations, to press them further toward delight and satisfaction in these ways of strictness. Thus the practisers themselves are not only confirmed in these customs and the opinions that go with them, but others are the more easily drawn to like and profess the same things. Any serious temper under any profession of religion easily becomes devout, and readily seizes opportunities to show its devotion through strictness. Therefore we find among the heathens a great devotional severity, far exceeding anything of that kind the Papists usually boast of. The Magi abstained from wine, ate no flesh of living creatures, and professed virginity. The Indian Brahmans did the same and, besides, subjected themselves to incredible hardship. They lay on skins, endured the violence of the sun and storms, and trained themselves in this way, some spending thirty-seven years in this course and others longer. We read strange things of this kind concerning the Egyptian priests and others. The Mahometans also have their religious orders, which claim a holier and more austere life than others. Although several private villainies are reported of some of them (such as the Torlachs and Dervishes), of others (such as the order of the Calenders) we are assured by history that they profess virginity, expose themselves to hardship, and practise a stricter devotion in their way. It is generally said of all of them that they go meanly clad, or half naked. Some are abstinent in eating and drinking, professing poverty and renouncing the world. Some can endure cutting and slashing as if they were insensible. Some profess perpetual silence even when provoked with injuries and tortures. Others wear chains on their necks and arms to show that they are bound off from the world, and so on. If such things may be found among heathens, it is no wonder that error boasts of them, for both rest on the same reason: people pleasing themselves in such hardships, which arises from a natural devotion assisted by Satan's cunning, and the same design is driven forward by it. For the Devil confirms heathens and Mahometans in their false worship through the reverence and respect they give to such practices.

units.la: Sixthly, A more plausible Argument for Errour (than the Learning and Holiness of the Persons that profess it) is that of Inspiration, in which the Devil soars a loft, and pretends the highest divine warrant for his falshoods: for God is Truth, and we know that no lye is of the Truth. Now to make Men believe that God by his Holy Spirit doth in any manner dictate such Opinions,or certainly reveal such things for Truths: is one of the highest Artifices that he can pretend to, and such a confirmation must it be (to those that are so perswaded,) that all disputes and doubtings must necessarily be silenced.
units.tr: Sixthly, a more plausible argument for error (more plausible than the learning and holiness of those who profess it) is that of inspiration. Here the Devil soars aloft and claims the highest divine warrant for his falsehoods, since God is truth, and we know that no lie is of the truth. To make men believe that God, by his Holy Spirit, in any way dictates such opinions, or certainly reveals such things as truths, is one of the highest artifices he can attempt. To those who are so persuaded, such a confirmation must silence all disputes and doubts.

units.la: That the Devil can thus transform himself into an Angel of Light, we are assured from Scripture, which hath particularly cautioned us against this cheat. The Apostacy of the later times, 1 Tim. 4. 1. the Apostle foretells should be carried on by the prevalency of this pretence, Some shall depart from the Faith, giving heed to seducing Spirits. That by Spirits there, Doctrines are intended rather than Doctors, is Mr. Medes interpretation: but it will come all to one if we consider that the word Spirit carryes more in it, than either Doctrine or Doctor; for to call either the one or the other a Spirit ... would be intollerably harsh, if it were not for this, that that Doctor is hereby supposed to pretend an infallibility from the Spirit of God, or (which is all one) that he received his Doctrine by some immediate Revelation of the Spirit ; so that by feducing Spirits must be, Men or Doctrines that feduce others to believe them, by the pretence of the Spirit, or Inspiration : and that text of 1 Joh. 4. 1. doth thus explain it, believe not every Spirit, but try the Spirits whether they are of God ; which is as much as if he had said, believe not every Man or Doctrine that shall pretend he is fent of God, and hath his Spirit ; and the reason there given makes it yet more plain, because many false Prophets are gone out into the World : So that these Spirits are false Prophets, Men that pretend inspiration. And the warning, believe not every Spirit,tells us, that Satan doth with such a dexterity counterfeit the Spirits Inspirations, that holy and good Men are in no small hazard to be deceived thereby. Most full to this purpose is that of 2 Thess. 2.2. That ye be not soon shaken in Mind, or be troubled, neither by Spirit, nor by Word, nor by Letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand ; where the several means of feduction are particularly reckoned, as distinct from the Doctrine and Doctors, and by Spirit can be meant no other than a pretence of Inspiration or Revelation.
units.tr: That the Devil can thus transform himself into an angel of light, we are assured from Scripture, which has particularly warned us against this deception. The Apostle foretells in 1 Tim. 4. 1 that the apostasy of later times will be carried on by the prevalence of this pretence: Some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits. Mr. Mede's interpretation is that by spirits here doctrines are meant rather than doctors. But it comes to the same thing if we consider that the word spirit carries more meaning than either doctrine or doctor. To call either one or the other a spirit would be intolerably harsh, were it not that the doctor is thereby supposed to claim an infallibility from the Spirit of God, or (which is the same thing) to have received his doctrine by some immediate revelation of the Spirit. So by seducing spirits must be meant men or doctrines that seduce others into believing them by the pretence of the Spirit, or inspiration. The text of 1 John 4. 1 explains it the same way: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God. This is as much as to say, believe not every man or doctrine that shall pretend he is sent of God and has his Spirit. The reason given there makes it plainer still: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. So these spirits are false prophets, men who pretend to inspiration. And the warning, believe not every spirit, tells us that Satan counterfeits the Spirit's inspirations with such dexterity that holy and good men are in no small danger of being deceived by them. Most full to this purpose is 2 Thess. 2. 2: That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. Here the several means of seduction are listed separately from the doctrine and the doctors, and by spirit can be meant nothing other than a pretence of inspiration or revelation.

units.la: If we trace Satan in the Errours which he hath raised up under the profession of the Scriptures, we may observe the same method, the Valentinians, Gnosticks, Montanists talked as confidently of the Spirit, as Moses or the Prophets could do, and a great deal more; for some of them blasphemously called themselves the Paraclete, or Comforter. Among the Monsters which later Ages produced, we still find the same strain; one faith he is Enoch, another stiles himself the great Prophet, another hath raptures, and all immediately inspired. The Papists have as much of this cheat among them as any other, and some of their learned Defenders avouch their Lumen Propheticum, and Miraculorum Gloria, Prophesies and Miracles, to be the two eyes, or the Sun and Moon of their Church; nay by a strange transportment of Folly, (to the forfeiture of the reputation of Learning and Reason) they have so multiplied Revelations, that we have whole Volumns of them, as the Revelations of their Saint Brigit and others; and by wonderful credulity they have not only advanced apparent dreams and dotages to the honour of Inspirations or Visions, but upon this sandy Foundation they have built a great many of their Doctrines, as Purgatory, Transubstantiation, auricular Confession, &c. By such warrants have they instituted Festivals, and founded several Orders; the particulars of these things you may see more at large in Dr. Stillingfleet and others. And that there might be nothing wanting that might make them shamelesly impudent, they are not content to equal their Fooleries with the Scriptures of God, as that the rule of their St. Francis (for I shall only instance in him, omitting others for brevity sake) was not composed by the Wisdom of Man, but by God himself, and inspired by the Holy Ghost; but they advance their Prophets above the Apostles, and above Christ himself. Their St. Benedict (if you will believe them) was rapt up to the third Heavens, where he saw God Face to Face, and heard the choire of Angels; and their St. Francis was a none-such for Miracles and Revelations. Neither may we wonder that Satan should be forward in urging this cheat, when we consider,
units.tr: If we trace Satan in the errors he has raised up under the profession of the Scriptures, we see the same method. The Valentinians, Gnostics and Montanists talked as confidently of the Spirit as Moses or the prophets could do, and far more so, for some of them blasphemously called themselves the Paraclete, or Comforter. Among the monsters that later ages produced we still find the same strain. One claims to be Enoch, another styles himself the great Prophet, another has raptures, and all are immediately inspired. The Papists have as much of this deception among them as any others. Some of their learned defenders avouch their Lumen Propheticum and Miraculorum Gloria, prophecies and miracles, to be the two eyes, or the sun and moon, of their Church. Nay, by a strange transport of folly, to the forfeiture of their reputation for learning and reason, they have so multiplied revelations that we have whole volumes of them, such as the revelations of their Saint Bridget and others. By wonderful credulity they have not only raised plain dreams and dotages to the honour of inspirations or visions, but upon this sandy foundation they have built a great many of their doctrines, such as purgatory, transubstantiation, auricular confession, &c. By such warrants they have instituted festivals and founded several orders. The particulars of these things may be seen more fully in Dr. Stillingfleet and others. And lest anything should be lacking to make them shamelessly impudent, they are not content to equal their follies with the Scriptures of God. Their rule of St. Francis (I shall mention only him, omitting others for brevity) was not composed by the wisdom of man, but by God himself, and inspired by the Holy Ghost. They even raise their prophets above the Apostles, and above Christ himself. Their St. Benedict (if we are to believe them) was caught up to the third heaven, where he saw God face to face and heard the choir of angels. Their St. Francis was a nonpareil for miracles and revelations. Nor need we wonder that Satan should be forward in urging this deception, when we consider:

units.la: For their antiquity and strangeness of discovery, especially at such times wherein the present posture of Affairs seem to favour such predictions with a probability of such events, are more likely to get credit, than these artificial imitations of the Ways and Garbs of the old Prophets, and the cunning Legerdemain of those that pretend to Inspirations, by seeming Extasies, Raptures, and confident Declarations, &c. nevertheless arrant Cheats, have by these ways deceived no mean Men. Alvarus acknowledgeth that he honoured a Woman as a Saint, that had Visions and Raptures, as if really inspired (and the same apprehensions had the Bishop and Fryars) who was afterward discovered to be a naughty Woman: who shall then think it strange that the unobservant Multitude should be deluded by such an Art?
units.tr: For their antiquity and the strangeness of their discovery, especially at such times when the present posture of affairs seems to favour such predictions with a probability of such events, are more likely to win credit than those artificial imitations of the ways and garb of the old prophets, and the cunning sleight of hand of those who pretend to inspiration by seeming ecstasies, raptures, and confident declarations, etc. Yet these arrant cheats have by such means deceived no mean men. Alvarus acknowledges that he honoured as a saint a woman who had visions and raptures, as if she were truly inspired (and the bishop and friars had the same impressions), who was afterwards discovered to be a wicked woman. Who then will think it strange that the unobservant multitude should be deluded by such an art?

units.la: Seventhly, Pretended and counterfeit Miracles the Devil makes much use of, to countenance Errour, and this is also one of his strong-holds; for he suggests that God himself bears witness by these Signs, Wonders,and Miracles to such erroneous Doctrine, as seems to be concerned by them.
units.tr: Seventhly, the Devil makes much use of pretended and counterfeit miracles to support error, and this is also one of his strongholds. He suggests that God himself bears witness by these signs, wonders, and miracles to such erroneous doctrine as seems to be backed by them.

units.la: That the Devil cannot work a true Miracle hath been discourfed before, but that he can perform many strange things, and such as may beget admiration, none denies; and that by such unwonted actions, he usually endeavours to justify false Doctrines, and to set them off with the appearance of divine approbation, we are sufficiently forewarned in the Scriptures. Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses by false Miracles. In Deut. 13. 1. God speaks of the Signs and Wonders of false Prophets, who would by that means seek to seduce the People to follow after other Gods. Christ also in Matth. 24.24. foretells that false Christs and false Prophets shall arise, and shew great Signs and Wonders, insomuch that (if it were possible) they shall deceive the very Elect, and puts a special note of caution upon it, Behold, I have told you before. And to the same purpose is that of Paul concerning Antichrist, 2 Thes. 2.9. where he tells us of powerful Signs and Wonders by the working of Satan; who doth all the while only lye and cheat, that he may draw Men to Errour.
units.tr: That the Devil cannot work a true miracle has been discussed before, but that he can perform many strange things, such as may beget admiration, no one denies. We are sufficiently forewarned in the Scriptures that by such unusual actions he commonly endeavours to justify false doctrines and to set them off with the appearance of divine approval. Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses by false miracles. In Deut. 13. 1, God speaks of the signs and wonders of false prophets, who by that means would seek to seduce the people to follow other gods. Christ also, in Matth. 24.24, foretells that false Christs and false prophets shall arise, and shall show great signs and wonders, insomuch that (if it were possible) they shall deceive the very elect, and he puts a special note of caution upon it: Behold, I have told you before. To the same purpose is Paul's word concerning Antichrist, 2 Thes. 2.9, where he speaks of powerful signs and wonders wrought by the working of Satan, who all the while does nothing but lie and cheat, that he may draw men into error.

units.la: As to the first of these, 'tis evident, that a great many things, that have been taken by the vulgar for mighty Wonders, were nothing but the knaveries of Impostors, who in this matter have used a threefold cunning.
units.tr: As to the first of these, it is evident that many things which the common people took for mighty wonders were nothing but knaveries of impostors, who in this matter have used a threefold cunning.

units.la: First, By meer jugling and Forgery in confederacies and private contrivances they have set upon the Stage Persons (before instructed to act their parts) or things aforehand prepared, to pretend to be what they were not, that others might seem to do what they did not, and all to amaze those that know not the bottom of the matter. Of this nature was Mahomets Dove and Bull, who were privately trained up to that obedience, and familiarity which they used to him. The Pagan Priests were not altogether to seek in this peice of art. Lucian tells us of one Alexander, who nourished and tamed a Serpent, and made the People of Pontus believe that it was the God Æsculapius; and doubtless the Idol Priests improved their private artificial contrivances. As of the movings of their Images (as that of Venus made by Dædalus, which by the means of Quicksilver inclosed, could stir it self) their eating and drinking (as in the Story of Bel in the Apochryphal adjections to the Book of Daniel) their responses, and several other appearances (as of the Paper Head of Adonis or Osiris) which (as Lucian reports) comes swimming down the River every year from Ægypt to Byblos, &c. these and such like they improved as evidences of the Power, Knowledg, and reality of their Gods. And though in the prevalency of Idolatry, where there was no considerable party to oppose, their cheats were not always discovered, yet we have no reason to imagine that the Priests of those days were so honest, that they were only deceived by the Devils craft, and did not in a villanous design purposely indeavour the delusion of others. If we had no other grounds for a just suspition in these cases, the famous instances of the abuse of Paulina at the Temple of Isis in Rome, in the Reign of the Emperour Tyberius, by the procurement of Mondus, who corrupted the Priest of Anubis to signify to her the love of their God, and under that coverture gratified the Lust of Mondus, mentioned by Josephus. And that of Tyrannus Priest of Saturne in Alexandria, who by the like pretence of the love of Saturne, adulterated most of the fairest Dames of the City, mentioned by Ruffinus. These would sufficiently witness that the Priests of those times were apt enough to abuse the people at the rate we have been speaking of. In Popery nothing hath been more ordinary ; who knows not the Story of the Holy Maid of Kent, and the Boy of Bilson ? How common is it with them to play tricks with Women troubled with Hysterical Distempers ? and to pretend the casting out of Devils, when they have only to deal with a natural Disease ? Not very many years since they practised upon a poor young Woman at Durham, and made great boasts of their Exorcisms, Reliques, and Holy-water against the Devil (with whom they would have all believe she was possessed) when the event discovered, that her Fits were only the Fits of the Mother. I my self (and some others in this place) have seen those Fits allayed by the Fume of Tobacco blown into her Mouth, to the shame and apparent detection of that Artifice. I might mention the Legerdemain of Antonius of Padua, who made his Horse adore the Host, for the conversion of an Heretick ; the finding of the Images of St. Paul and St. Dominick, in a Church at Venice with this Inscription for Paul, By this Man you may come to Christ ; and this for Dominick, But by this Man you may do it easilier : and the Honour put upon Garnet, by his Image on Straw, found at his Execution, (in all probability) by him that made it and threw it down, or by his Confederate : but these are enough to shew the honesty of these kind of Men.
units.tr: First, by sheer juggling and forgery, through confederacies and private contrivances, they have brought onto the stage persons (before instructed to act their parts) or things aforehand prepared, to pretend to be what they were not, so that others might seem to do what they did not, and all to amaze those who do not know the bottom of the matter. Of this kind was Mahomet's dove and bull, which were privately trained up to that obedience and familiarity they showed him. The pagan priests were not at all at a loss in this piece of art. Lucian tells us of one Alexander who nourished and tamed a serpent and made the people of Pontus believe it was the god Aesculapius. Doubtless the idol priests improved their private artificial contrivances: the movings of their images (such as the Venus made by Daedalus, which by means of enclosed quicksilver could stir itself), their eating and drinking (as in the story of Bel in the apocryphal additions to the Book of Daniel), their responses, and several other appearances (such as the paper head of Adonis or Osiris which, as Lucian reports, came swimming down the river every year from Egypt to Byblos), and so on. These and the like they used as evidences of the power, knowledge and reality of their gods. And although, where idolatry had the upper hand and no considerable party was there to oppose it, their cheats were not always discovered, we have no reason to imagine that the priests of those days were so honest that they were only deceived by the devil's craft and did not, in a villanous design, purposely endeavour to delude others. Even if we had no other grounds for a just suspicion in these cases, there are the famous instances: the abuse of Paulina at the temple of Isis in Rome in the reign of the Emperor Tiberius, by the procurement of Mundus, who corrupted the priest of Anubis to signify to her the love of their god, and under that cover gratified the lust of Mundus, as Josephus mentions; and that of Tyrannus, priest of Saturn in Alexandria, who by the like pretence of the love of Saturn adulterated most of the fairest dames of the city, as Rufinus mentions. These would sufficiently witness that the priests of those times were apt enough to abuse the people in the way we have been speaking of. In Popery nothing has been more ordinary. Who does not know the story of the Holy Maid of Kent and the Boy of Bilson? How common is it with them to play tricks on women troubled with Hysterical distempers, and to pretend to cast out devils when they have only to deal with a natural disease? Not many years ago they practised upon a poor young woman at Durham, and made great boasts of their Exorcisms, Reliques and Holy-water against the devil (with whom they would have everyone believe she was possessed), when the outcome showed that her fits were only the fits of the Mother. I myself (and some others in this place) have seen those fits allayed by tobacco smoke blown into her mouth, to the shame and plain exposure of that artifice. I might mention the legerdemain of Anthony of Padua, who made his horse adore the Host for the conversion of a heretic; the finding of images of St. Paul and St. Dominick in a church at Venice, with this inscription under Paul, By this man you may come to Christ, and under Dominick, But by this man you may do it more easily; and the honour put upon Garnet by his image made of straw, found at his execution, in all probability by the one who made it and threw it down, or by his confederate. But these are enough to show the honesty of these kinds of men.

units.la: Secondly, They have also a cunning of ascribing effects to wrong causes, and by that means they make those things Wonders that are none. Mahomet called his Fits of Falling-Sickness, Extas-ies or Trances. Austin tells us the Heathens were notable at this: the burning Lamp in the Temple of Venus, though only the work of Art, was interpreted to be a constant Miracle of that Deity. The Image which (in another Temple) hung in the Air, by ignorant Gazers was accounted a Wonder, when indeed the Loadstone in the Roof and Pavement (though unseen) was the cause of it.
units.tr: Secondly, they also have a cunning of ascribing effects to wrong causes, and by that means they make things into wonders which are none. Mahomet called his fits of falling sickness Extasies or trances. Augustine tells us the heathens were notable at this: the burning lamp in the temple of Venus, though only the work of art, was interpreted as a constant miracle of that deity. The image which (in another temple) hung in the air was accounted a wonder by ignorant gazers, when indeed the loadstone in the roof and pavement (though unseen) was the cause of it.

units.la: The Sydonians were confirmed in their constant annual Lamentations of Adonis, by a mock Miracle of the redness of the River Adonis, at one time of the year constantly, they take it to be Blood, when it is nothing else but the colouring of the Water by the dust of red Earth or Minium, which the Winds constantly at that time of the year from Mount Libanus do drive into the Water. Neither are the Papists out in this point; I will only instance in that observation of Dr. Jenison, to confirm the Doctrine and Practice of Invocation: they take the advantage of Sovereign Baths and Waters, and where they espy any Fountain good against the Stone, or other Diseases, presently there is the Statue or Image of some Saint or other erected by it, by whose Vertue the Cure and Miracle must seem to be done; or some Chappel is erected to this or that Saint, to whom Prayers before, and thanks after washing, must be offered.
units.tr: The Sidonians were confirmed in their constant annual lamentations for Adonis by a mock miracle: at one time of the year the river Adonis constantly turns red, and they take it to be blood, when it is nothing but the colouring of the water by the dust of red earth or minium, which at that time of year the winds constantly drive from Mount Libanus into the water. Nor are the Papists wrong in this point. I will only instance that observation of Dr. Jenison, to confirm the doctrine and practice of Invocation: they take advantage of sovereign Baths and Waters, and wherever they espy any fountain good against the stone or other diseases, at once a statue or image of some saint or other is set up beside it, by whose vertue the cure and miracle must seem to be done; or a chappel is built to this or that saint, to whom prayers must be offered beforehand and thanks after washing.

units.la: Secondly, Because Satan hath a more than ordinary advantage to feign Miracles he doth more industriously set himself to pretend them, and to urge them, for the accomplishment of his ends. ’Tis an easy work to prevail with Men that are wholly devoted to their own Inter-est under the Mask of Religion, to say and do any thing that may further their design; and the business of Miracles is so imitable by Art, through the ignorance and heedlesness of Men, that with a small labour Satan can do it at pleasure. The secret Powers of Nature (such as that of the Loadstone) by a dexterous application brought into act, in a fitly contrived Subject, will seem Miraculous to those that see not the secret springs of those actions. There have been artificial contrivances of Motions, which had they been disguised under a religious form, and directed to such an end, might have passed for greater Miracles than many which we have mentioned. Such was the Dove of Architas which did fly in the Air, as if it had been a living Creature. Such was the Flie of Regiomontanus, and the Eagle presented to the Emperour Maximilan, which in the compas of their little Bodies, contained so many Springs and Wheels as were sufficient to give them Motion, and to direct their courses as if they had been animated. Albertus Magnus his Artificial Man, and the Silver Gally, and Tritons made by a Goldsmith at Paris, were rare peices of Art, their Motions so certain and steady, that they seemed to have Life and Understanding. If Art can do all this, how much more may we suppose can Satan do? how easily can he make Apparitions, present strange Sights to the Eye, and Voices to the Ear? and by putting out his Power do a thousand things astonishing and wonderful?
units.tr: Secondly, because Satan has a more than ordinary advantage in feigning miracles. He sets himself more diligently to pretend them and to urge them for the accomplishment of his ends. It is an easy task to prevail upon men who are wholly devoted to their own interest under the mask of religion to say and do anything that may further their design, and the business of miracles is so imitable by art, through the ignorance and heedlessness of men, that with little labour Satan can do it at will. The secret powers of nature (such as that of the loadstone), brought into action by a dexterous application in a skilfully contrived subject, will seem miraculous to those who do not see the secret springs of those actions. There have been artificial contrivances of motion which, had they been disguised under a religious form and directed to such an end, might have passed for greater miracles than many we have mentioned. Such was the dove of Archytas, which flew in the air as if it were a living creature. Such was the fly of Regiomontanus, and the eagle presented to the Emperor Maximilian, which within the compass of their little bodies contained so many springs and wheels as were sufficient to give them motion and to direct their courses as if they were animated. Albertus Magnus his artificial man, and the silver galley and tritons made by a goldsmith at Paris, were rare pieces of art; their motions were so certain and steady that they seemed to have life and understanding. If art can do all this, how much more may we suppose Satan can do? How easily can he make apparitions, present strange sights to the eye and voices to the ear, and, by putting forth his power, do a thousand astonishing and wonderful things?

units.la: First, From inward Peace, and contentment of Mind. Satan knows that Peace is the thing to which a Man sacrificeth all his labours and travel; this he seeks, (though often in a wrong way, and by wrong means:) he knows also that true Peace is only the Daughter of Truth, (the ways whereof are pleasantness, and the Paths whereof are Peace;) neither is he ignorant of the delights which a Man hath, by enjoying himself in the sweet repose of a contented Mind, that he may charm the Hearts of the erroneous into a confidence and assurance that they have taken a right course, he doth all he can to further a false peace in them, and to this purpose he commonly useth this method:
units.tr: First, on inward peace and contentment of mind. Satan knows that peace is the thing for which a man sacrifices all his labours and toil; this he seeks, though often in a wrong way and by wrong means. He knows also that true peace is only the daughter of truth (the ways whereof are pleasantness, and the paths whereof are peace), and he is not ignorant of the delight a man finds in the sweet repose of a contented mind. So that he may charm the hearts of the erroneous into confidence that they have taken the right course, he does all he can to foster a false peace in them, and to this end he commonly uses this method:

units.la: Secondly, His second approach is to raise a storm of restless disquiet upon that uncertainty; and in order to his intended design he usually fills them with the utmost anxiety of Mind, and makes their Thoughts (like a tempestuous Sea) dash one against an-other. This piece of his Art is noted in the forecited place, that ye be not shaken in mind or troubled; the word signifies a great perplexity. And this is an usual method which the false Teachers among the Galatians practised, they first troubled them, and then endeavoured by the advantage of that trouble to pervert the Gospel of Christ. To effect both these, he doth amuse them with all the objections that can be raised. If he can say any thing of the Antiquity of the Errour, the Number, Wisdom, Learning or Authority of those that embrace it, they are sure to hear of these things to the full; the danger of continuing as they were, and the happiness of the new Doctrine, are represented with all aggravating circumstances; and these so often, that their thoughts have no rest: and if this restlesnes does wound or weaken them, he pursues with an high hand. These ways of disturbing the unsettled mind, are hinted to us in the aforesaid place, Spirit, Word, Letter, any thing that carries a seeming Authority to unsettle, or power to amaze and distress. And we may here further note, that where the minds of Men are discomposed with other fears or disquiets, Satan is ready to improve them to this use, so that commonly when the Word of God begins to work at first upon the consciences of Men, to awaken them to the consideration of their Sin and Danger, the Adversary is then very busy with them to inveagle them into some Errour or other.
units.tr: Secondly, his second approach is to raise a storm of restless disquiet upon that uncertainty. To this end he usually fills them with the utmost anxiety of mind, and makes their thoughts, like a tempestuous sea, dash against one another. This part of his craft is noted in the place cited above, that ye be not shaken in mind or troubled; the word signifies great perplexity. This was a usual method of the false teachers among the Galatians: they first troubled them, and then tried, by the advantage of that trouble, to pervert the gospel of Christ. To achieve both, he plies them with every objection that can be raised. If he can say anything of the antiquity of the error, or of the number, wisdom, learning or authority of those who embrace it, they are sure to hear all of it; the danger of remaining as they were and the happiness of the new doctrine are presented with every aggravating circumstance, and these so often that their thoughts have no rest. If this restlessness wounds or weakens them, he presses on with a high hand. These ways of disturbing the unsettled mind are hinted at in the aforesaid place: spirit, word, letter, anything that carries a seeming authority to unsettle, or power to amaze and distress. We may further note here that where men's minds are disturbed by other fears or disquiets, Satan is ready to turn them to this use. So commonly, when the Word of God first begins to work upon men's consciences, awakening them to consideration of their sin and danger, the Adversary is then very busy to entangle them in some error or other.

units.la: Thirdly, Having throughly prepared the mind with restless fears, he then advanceth forward with the proffers of peace and comfort in the way of Errour which he proposeth;and in this case Errour will boast much,Come to me,and ye shall find rest for your souls. How grateful and welcome the confident proffers of ease and satisfaction areto a tossed and disquieted mind any Man will easily imagine? 'Tis usually thus, Men that are tired out, will easily embrace any thing for ease. A Man in this case may be wrought upon like Wax to receive any Impression; he will fasten on any thing true or false that doth but promise comfort.
units.tr: Thirdly, having thoroughly prepared the mind with restless fears, he then advances with the offers of peace and comfort in the way of error which he proposes; and in this case error will boast much: Come unto me, and ye shall find rest for your souls. How welcome the confident offers of ease and satisfaction are to a tossed and disquieted mind, anyone can easily imagine. Men who are worn out will readily embrace anything for ease. A man in this state may be worked upon like wax to receive any impression; he will fasten on anything, true or false, that promises comfort.

units.la: Secondly, Outward prosperity is the other common plea for Errour. Though successes,plenty and abundance of worldly comforts, argue of themselves neither love nor hatred, truth nor falshood, because the wise Providence of God, for holy ends and reasons (often undiscerned by us) permits often the Tabernacles of Robbers to prosper, and permits those that deal treacherously with the Truths of God, to be planted, to take root, to grow, yea, to bring forth Fruit; nevertheless it in a way of Errour they meet with outward Blessings, they are apt to ascribe all to their Errours, and to say as Israel, Hos. 2. 5. I will go after my Lovers that gave me my Bread and my Water, my Wool and my Flax, mine Oyl and my Drink, without any serious consideration of God's common Bounty, which upon far other accounts, gives them Corn, and Wine, and Oyl, and multiplies their Silver and Gold, which they prepared for Baal, ver. 8. I shall not need to add any thing further for the proof and explanation of this, than what we have in Jer. 44. 17. where the Jews expresly advance their Idolatrous Worship as the right way, and confirm themselves even to obstinacy in the pursuit of it, upon this reason; We will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth out of our own Mouth, to burn Incense to the Queen of Heaven — for then had we plenty of Victuals, and were well, and saw no evil: but since we left off to burn Incense to the Queen of Heaven, and to pour out our drink-offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the Sword, and by the Famine.
units.tr: Secondly, outward prosperity is the other common plea for error. Yet success, plenty and abundance of worldly comforts argue of themselves neither love nor hatred, neither truth nor falsehood. God's wise providence, for holy ends and reasons (often undiscerned by us), often permits the tabernacles of robbers to prosper, and permits those that deal treacherously with the truths of God to be planted, to take root, to grow, yea, to bring forth fruit. Nevertheless, if in a way of error men meet with outward blessings, they are apt to ascribe all to their errors and to say, as Israel did, Hos. 2. 5., I will go after my lovers that gave me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink, without any serious consideration of God's common bounty, which on quite other grounds gives them corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplies their silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal, ver. 8. I need add nothing further for the proof and explanation of this than what we have in Jer. 44. 17., where the Jews expressly advance their idolatrous worship as the right way and confirm themselves even to obstinacy in pursuing it, on this reason: We will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth out of our own mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven ... for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil: but since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink-offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.

units.la: Ninthly, Instead of better arguments, Satan usually makes Lyes his refuge: and these respect either the Truth which he would cry down, or the Errour which he would set up.
units.tr: Ninthly, instead of better arguments, Satan usually takes refuge in lies, and these concern either the truth he would cry down or the error he would set up.

units.la: Those Lyes that are managed against Truth, are of two sorts; mistakes and misrepresentations of its Doctrines, or Calumnies against the Persons and Actions of those that take part with it.
units.tr: Lies told against truth are of two kinds: misrepresentations of its doctrines, or calumnies against the persons and actions of those who take its part.

units.la: As for calumnies against the Persons and Actions of those that are Assertors of Truth, 'tis well known for an old thread-bare design, by which Satan hath gained not a little. Machiavil borrowed the policy from him, and formed it into a Maxime, for he found by experience that where strong Slanders had set in their Teeth, though never so unjustly, the Wounds were never throughly healed: for some that heard the report of the Slander, never heard the Vindication, and those that did, were not always so unprejudiced as to free themselves from all suspition, but still something remained usually upon their Spirits for ever after; and that, like a secret venome, poysons all that could be said or done by the Persons, that ( wrongfully ) fell under their prejudice, and did not a little derogate from the authority and power of the Truths which they delivered.
units.tr: As for calumnies against the persons and actions of those who assert the truth, it is well known as an old, threadbare design, by which Satan has gained not a little. Machiavelli borrowed the policy from him and turned it into a maxim, for he found by experience that where strong slanders had got their teeth in, however unjust, the wounds were never thoroughly healed. Some who heard the report of the slander never heard the vindication, and those who did were not always so unprejudiced as to free themselves from all suspicion. Something usually remained upon their spirits for ever after, and that, like a secret venom, poisons all that could be said or done by the persons who, wrongfully, fell under their prejudice, and it does not a little derogate from the authority and power of the truths they delivered.

units.la: The Friends of Truth have always to their cost found it so. Christ himself escaped not the lyes and censures of Men when he did the greatest Miracles; they raised this calumny against him, That he cast out Devils by Beelzebub the Prince of Devils: when he shewed the most compassionate condescentions, they called him a Man gluttonous, a Wine-bibber, a friend of Publicans and Sinners; and at last upon a misinterpretation of his speeches, ( I will destroy this Temple, and in three days I will build it up, Mat. 26.61. ) they arraigned and condemned him for Blasphemy: and his Servants have ( according to what he foretold ) drunk of the same Cup; the more eminent in service, the greater draught. Paul, a chosen vessel,met with much of this unjust dealing; he was accused Act. 21.28. as speaking against the People, the Law, and the Temple; and, Chap. 24.5. called a pestilent Fellow, a mover of Sedition, a prophaner of the Temple. Neither can we wonder at this, that the greatest Innocency, or highest degree of Holiness, is no Armour of proof against the sharp Arrows of a lying Tongue: When we read this as one of Satan's great Characters, that he is the Accuser of the Brethren, and that his Agents are so perfectly instructed in this Art, that they are also branded with the same mark of false Accusers, Jude 10. 'Tis well known how the Primitive Christians were used, they were accounted the filth and off-scouring of all things; there could be nothing that could render them odious or ridiculous but they were aspersed with it, as that they sacrificed Infants, worshipped the Sun, and used promiscuous Uncleannesse; nay, what ever Plague or disaster befel their Neighbours, they were sure to carry the blame. And we might trace this Stratagem down to our own days. Luther in his time was the common Butt for all the poysoned Arrows of the Papists calumny; which so exceeded all bounds of Sobriety and Prudence, that they devised a Romance of his Death, how he was choaked of the Devil; that before he died, he desired his Corps might be carried into the Church,and adored with divine Worship; and that after his Death the excessive stench of his Carcase forced all his Friends to forsake him. All this and more to this purpose they published while he was alive, whose Slanders (worthy only of laughter) he refuted by his own Pen. The like fury they expressed against Calvin, by their Bolsecus, whom they set on work to fill a Book with impudent lyes against him: Neither did Beza, Junius, or any other of note escape without some slander or other. How unjustly the Arrians of old accused Athanasius of Uncleanness, and of bereaving Arsenius of his Arm, is sufficiently known in History.
units.tr: The friends of truth have always found this to their cost. Christ himself did not escape the lies and censures of men, even when he worked the greatest miracles. They raised this calumny against him: That he cast out devils by Beelzebub the Prince of Devils. When he showed the most compassionate condescension, they called him a gluttonous man, a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. And at last, on a misinterpretation of his words (Destroy this temple, and in three days I will build it up, Matt. 26.61), they arraigned and condemned him for blasphemy. His servants, as he foretold, have drunk of the same cup, the more eminent in service taking the greater draught. Paul, a chosen vessel, met with much of this unjust dealing. He was accused (Acts 21.28) of speaking against the people, the law and the temple, and (Acts 24.5) was called a pestilent fellow, a mover of sedition, a profaner of the temple. Nor can we wonder that the greatest innocence or the highest degree of holiness is no armour of proof against the sharp arrows of a lying tongue. We read that Satan is the accuser of the brethren*, one of his great marks, and his agents are so perfectly instructed in this art that they too bear the same brand of false accusers (Jude 10). It is well known how the primitive Christians were treated: they were counted the filth and off-scouring of all things. There was nothing that could render them odious or ridiculous with which they were not charged: that they sacrificed infants, worshipped the sun, and practised promiscuous uncleanness. Nay, whatever plague or disaster befell their neighbours, they were sure to bear the blame. We might trace this stratagem down to our own days. Luther in his time was the common butt for all the poisoned arrows of Papist calumny, which so exceeded all bounds of sobriety and prudence that they devised a romance of his death: how he was choked by the devil; how before he died he asked that his corpse be carried into the church and adored with divine worship; and how after his death the excessive stench of his carcase forced all his friends to forsake him. All this, and more to the same purpose, they published while he was alive, and he refuted these slanders, worthy only of laughter, with his own pen. The same fury they showed against Calvin through their Bolsec, whom they set to work filling a book with shameless lies against him. Nor did Beza, Junius, or any other man of note escape without some slander or other. How unjustly the Arians of old accused Athanasius of uncleanness, and of robbing Arsenius of his arm, is sufficiently known from history.

units.la: As Satan's design in bespattering the Actions and Doctrines of good Men, is to bring the Truth they professe into a suspition of falshood, and to advance the contrary Errours to the place and credit of Truth; so doth he use a skill proportionable to his design. And though he be so impudent that he will not blush at the contrivance of the most gross and malicious lye, yet withall he is so cunning, that he studiously endeavours some probable rise for his slanders, and commonly he takes this course:

units.la: Thirdly, The least slip or infirmity of the Children of Truth the Devil is ready to bring upon the Stage; and they that will not charge themselves as offenders for very great evils, will yet object to the disparagement of Truth the smallest mistakes of others; a mote in the eye of the lovers of Truth shall be espyed, when abeam in the eye of falshood shall pass for nothing.
units.tr: Thirdly, the least slip or infirmity of the children of truth the Devil is ready to bring upon the stage. Those who will not charge themselves as offenders for very great evils will yet object to the disparagement of truth the smallest mistakes of others. A mote in the eye of the lovers of truth shall be espied, while a beam in the eye of falsehood shall pass for nothing.

units.la: Fourthly, Slanderous Aspersions are sometimes raised from a simple mistake of Actions, and their grounds or manner of performance, and sometimes from a malicious Misrepresentation. The Devil seldom acts from a simple mistake, but he will either suborn the passionate Oppofers to a wilful perverting of the true management of things, or will by a false account of things take the advantage of their prejudice, to make Men believe that such things have been said or done, which indeed never were. The Christians in the Primitive times were reported to be bloody Men, and that they did kill Men in Sacrifice, and did eat their Flesh and drink their Blood; and this was only occasioned by their Doctrine and use of the Sacrament of the Body and Blood of Christ. They were accused for promiscuous uncleanness with one another, and this only because they taught that there was no distinction of Male and Female in respect of Justification, and that they were all Brethren and Sisters in Christ. This account Tertullian gives of the Calumnies of those times, and others have noted the like occasions of other abuses of them. They were reported to worship the Sun, because they in times of persecution were forced to meet early in the Fields, and were often seen undispersed at Sunrising. They were reported to worship Bacchus and Ceres, because of the Elements of Bread and Wine in the Lords Supper. If they met in private places, and in the night, it was enough to occasion surmises of Conspiracy and Rebellion: so ready is Satan to take occasion where none is given.

The Devil seldom acts from a simple mistake; he will either suborn passionate opposers to a wilful perverting of the true management of things, or will, by a false account of things, take advantage of their prejudice to make men believe that such things have been said or done which indeed never were. The Christians in the primitive times were reported to be bloody men, who killed men in sacrifice and ate their flesh and drank their blood. This was occasioned only by their doctrine and use of the sacrament of the body and blood of Christ. They were accused of promiscuous uncleanness with one another, and this only because they taught that there was no distinction of male and female in respect of justification, and that they were all brethren and sisters in Christ. Tertullian gives this account of the calumnies of those times, and others have noted the like occasions of other abuses of them. They were reported to worship the sun, because in times of persecution they were forced to meet early in the fields, and were often seen still gathered at sunrise. They were reported to worship Bacchus and Ceres, because of the elements of bread and wine in the Lord's Supper. If they met in private places and at night, it was enough to occasion surmises of conspiracy and rebellion. So ready is Satan to take occasion where none is given.

units.la: These were the Lyes raised against Truth; but besides this endeavour, he useth the same Art of lying to inhance the credit of Errour. Lying Inspirations, Lying Signs and Wonders we have spoken of, I shall only mention another sort of Lying, which is that of Forgery, an Art which Errour hath commonly made use of. Sometimes Books and Writings erroneous have been made to carry the names of Men that never knew or saw them. The Apostles themselves escaped not these abuses; you read of the counterfeit Gospels of Thomas and Bartholomew, the Acts of Peter and Andrew, the Apostolical Constitutions, and a great many more. Later Writers have by the like hard usage been forced to father the Brats of other Mens Brains. I might be large in these, but they that please may see more of this in Authors, that have of purpose discovered the frauds of spurious, suppositious Books; the design is obvious; Errour would by this means adorn it self with the excellent names of Men of renown, that so it might pass for good Doctrine with the unwary.
